subject: Scaling by fixed loading and fixed latent variance

messages.author: 744ad518e240c51e
messages.subject: Scaling by fixed loading and fixed latent variance
parts:
Dear Lavaan users,

I have some confusion with the scaling method. In the model that I am working with, I have three latent variables, each of which has three indicators.

 

There are several ways that we can set the scale of the latent variable. By default, cfa() would fix the factor loading of the first indicator of each latent variable to 1. Like in the following example:

model<-'

updating =~ Task1 + Task4 + Task6

inhibition =~ Task9 + Task7 + Task3

shifting =~ Task2 + Task5 + Task8

'

fit.model.m <- cfa(model,estimator = "mlm",data = EF.data.M)

This model works fine.

 

Alternatively, we can set the variance of each latent variable to 1, this could be done by adding an input argument. So I did the following:

fit.model.alt.m <- cfa(model,estimator = "mlm",data = EF.data.M,std.lv = TRUE)

However, this time I am getting a warning message that covariance matrix of latent variable is not positive definite.

 

Another alternative is to specify the fixed latent variance in the model, so I did the following:

model.std.lv<-'

updating =~ NA*Task1 + Task4 + Task6

inhibition =~ NA*Task9 + Task7 + Task3

shifting =~ NA*Task2 + Task5 + Task8

updating ~~ 1*updating

inhibition ~~ 1*inhibition

shifting ~~ 1*shifting

'

fit.model.std.lv.m <- cfa(model.std.lv,estimator = "mlm",data = EF.data.M)

This time, I am having the same warning message that covariance matrix of latent variable is not positive definite.

 

I thought that the above three ways were equivalent, so I couldn't understand why they might lead to different results. Do you have any ideas why this is the case? Or am I making some mistakes with the models?

 

Many thanks in advance,

Beinan

Hi Yves,


Sure. Please see following the syntax and attached the data (data.scale1). Although I need to point out that this dataset is not the original one. As I used very different task measurements, the SDs varied a lot. I saw a thread suggesting scaling the variables (http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/61869/how-to-interpret-the-model-fit-indices-generated-by-lavaan-in-r-something-wro). Therefore I followed the suggestion and scaled the variables, so that the max(SD) < 10 min(SD).


Syntax

data.scale1 <- read.delim("…/data.scale1.txt", header=FALSE)

names(data.scale1)<- c("ID","Task1","Task2","Task3","Task4","Task5","Task6","Task7","Task8","Task9")

model <- '

inhibition =~ Task9 + Task7 + Task3

updating =~ Task1 + Task4 + Task6

shifting =~ Task2 + Task5 + Task8'

> fit.model.fix.loading <- cfa(model,estimator = "mlm",data = data.scale1)

> fit.model.fix.variance <- cfa(model,estimator = "mlm",data = data.scale1,std.lv = TRUE)

  

Covariance matrix

I inspected the covariance matrix and noticed that the covariance varied a lot. Is this a problem?

Scaling

So I tried re-scaling the dataset with different scalers (see data.scale2). After doing this both models converged with no warnings. Following is the new covariance matrix with data.scale2.

Task8  1.277  1.519  0.921  1.653  0.034  0.180  3.618  3.680  7.865

 

Do you think the scaling might be the problem? I mean scaling should not be problematic, as I tried several scaling, as long as the model converged successfully without warning, the fitting provided exact same results. But it appears to me that depending on the way data is scaled, there is chance that the fitting does not work well.


I am sorry for so many question, this is my first CFA attempt and I want to make sure I know what I am doing. Thanks again in advance!


Best,

Beinan

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Scaling by fixed loading and fixed latent variance
parts:
On 05/05/2015 07:00 PM, Beinan Zhou wrote:
> Do you think the scaling might be the problem?

Yes. It seems that the scales of the observed variables (between 1000
and 10000) are too far away from the scales of the latent variables (if
std.lv = TRUE). Usually, this always leads to non-convergence warnings,
but for some reason, not for this data.

Rescaling helps, of course, but I fully agree that this is most
unfortunate. lavaan needs a global strategy to become scale-independent.
I will make this a priority.

Yves.
